question.problem: What is the parametrization of the curve $r(t)=5\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,j-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,k,$  $\,t\ge 0,$ by its arc length $s?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and its magnitude $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t))k \\  & =5\cdot 4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,i-4\cdot 4\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\,j+3\cdot 4\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\,k \\  & =20\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\,i-16\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\,j+12\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(20\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t))}^{2}+{(16\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t))}^{2}+{(12\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{400{cos}^{2}⁡(4t)+256{sin}^{2}⁡(4t)+144{sin}^{2}⁡(4t)} \\  & =\sqrt{400[{cos}^{2}⁡(4t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(4t)]} \\  & =20\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the arc length of the curve from $0$ to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}s & ={\int }_{0}^{t}‖{r}^{′}(u)‖\,\text{d}u \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{t}20\,\text{d}u \\  & =20u\,{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =20t\end{aligned}
$$

  

Now, since $s=20t$, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}s & =20t \\ t & =\frac{s}{20}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector function that parametrizes $r(t)$ by its arc length is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}R(s) & =r(\frac{s}{20}) \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{s}{20})i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{s}{20})j-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{s}{20})k \\  & =5\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{5})i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})j-3\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{5})k.\end{aligned}
$$
